purpose: Hand-labeled cases for the Orchestrator's parse-and-route step. Graded by comparing the parse step's output (and the agents the code then picks) against 'expected'. The target is >=90% correct routing. Reviewed on 2026-09-30; the five judgment-call cases carry a 'reviewed' note with the decision.
routing_rules_assumed: request_type is one of: new_evaluation, provide_constraints, follow_up, out_of_scope, unclear.
new_evaluation with no narrowing: run regulations + competitive_analysis; also run model_stack_analysis only if at least one numeric constraint (accuracy, latency, budget) was stated.
If the user asks narrowly (only the regulatory question, only competitors, only the model), run only what was asked.
A vague word like 'fast' or 'cheap' is not a usable constraint; it does not trigger model_stack_analysis, and the system asks for a number.
provide_constraints (needs saved session state): run model_stack_analysis only, using the saved feature description.
follow_up (anything else after results) is not supported in the first version: no agents run and the user is told so.
unclear and out_of_scope: no agents run. unclear asks one clarifying question; out_of_scope says so politely.
One feature per request: if two features are described, ask which to start with.
Routing depends only on what the user asked, never on what a sub-agent later finds (e.g. a prohibited feature still routes to all agents; hiding the model pick happens afterwards, in code).

accept_option (needs saved session state): no agents run; code works out which option was meant and records the choice. A question or what-if about an option, or a request to change the options, is follow_up, never accept_option.

report_outcome (no saved session needed): no agents run; code finds the recommendation it belongs to and a small model extracts the figures, which the PM confirms before anything is saved. Targets, plans and expectations are never report_outcome.

rule_tests_not_routing: regulations classification 'prohibited' -> model stack pick is not shown, regulations finding leads, competitive analysis still shown but never framed as mitigating.
regulations classification 'high_risk' -> regulations finding shown first, model pick flagged as needing validation against the obligations.
synthesis output missing the regulations classification or the disclaimer -> caught by the code check, not shown to the user.
regulations classification 'analysis_failed' or 'insufficient_information' -> shown to the user as exactly that, never as a clean result.
